title: Continuous-belt open-carton rejection by body pinch
objective: On a continuously running friction-driven belt, identify physically open cartons, avoid their articulated top flaps, grasp the rigid body below the hinges, and transfer each open carton nearly level into a reject tray without spilling its free contents. Initially closed cartons must remain untouched and continue past the downstream line. Body-pinching is a proposed robotic alternative, not a manufacturer-prescribed reject sequence.
success_conditions: Score each carton and average. Open carton: 0.25 when opposed gripper-pad contacts are established on body walls below the hinges; 0.50 when the complete carton clears the belt by at least 20 mm with every content item retained; 0.75 when the body and all contents are inside the reject-tray footprint; 1.00 after complete release, at least 60 mm robot clearance, and uninterrupted 3.0 s stability. Closed carton: 1.00 only after crossing the downstream line on its original belt path without robot contact; otherwise 0. A content item crossing the rim and contacting the belt, tray exterior, table, or floor permanently caps that open carton at 0.50. A dropped carton scores 0. Closing an open carton and letting it pass is not rejection. Full aggregate score requires every open carton rejected and every closed carton passed. Grade state at 10 Hz using fresh observations; use separate 240 Hz physics traces to validate contact, collisions, hinge motion, and friction without making substep metrics grading conditions.
industrial_value: Industrial cartoners detect open flaps and reject affected cartons. The acquired manual documents a pneumatic push-rod reject, while another industrial source warns that air-blast rejection is unsuitable for open packages that could spill. This task evaluates careful robotic removal of spill-prone rejects, relevant to packaging inspection and hand-removal work, without claiming that sidewall lifting is an established manufacturer procedure.
dexterity: High: the gripper must synchronize with a translating carton, enter an 80 mm-tall body-access band beneath collision-enabled flaps, establish bilateral frictional contact, lift without rim strikes, preserve loose contents, and release without disturbing the deposited carton.

asset_plan: Use pinned Isaac Sim 6.1.0.0 and YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730. The pinned snapshot defines FINGER_OPEN=-0.04695 m in yam_arena/constants.py and independently tests a 0.094 m open gap in tests/test_constants.py, so use a representative FEFCO 0201-style carton measuring 120 x 70 x 110 mm externally; its 70 mm grasp width leaves 24 mm nominal jaw-gap margin. Author 2 mm rigid walls, four 2 mm collision-enabled hinged flaps with 0–105 degree travel, an 80 mm-tall unobstructed body grasp band below the hinge axes, and three free 18 mm, 8 g rigid contents. Use a 500 x 180 mm belt at an initial 40 mm/s and a 180 x 160 x 50 mm reject tray. Model the closed state with an explicit break-free magnetic-detent approximation whose measured threshold is disclosed as a modeling assumption. Build from primitives and gate development in order: stationary grasp/lift; stationary transfer, release, and 3 s dwell; moving open carton; untouched closed-carton passage; mixed stream. Convey by surface motion and friction only; never force carton velocity, write object state, weld a grasp, or disable essential collisions.
risk: Ready means the sourced mechanism and internally consistent geometry are sufficient for the first rigid-PhysX build, not that physical feasibility or novelty has been certified. Stop expansion if pinned-YAM traces do not show opposed pad contact, flap clearance, retained contents, stable transport, and release clearance. Novelty fails if flap interference and spill preservation do not alter outcomes relative to generic moving-object selection and pick-and-place. Rigid walls approximate corrugated compliance and must be disclosed. Required counterfactuals are no action, flap-only grasp, rough tilt, all-remove, all-ignore, closed-carton contact, and off-belt staging.
